title_ar: الشيخ الددو يفتي في مسألة الصعق الكهربائي للدواجن
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Gives a Fatwa on the Question of the Electrical Stunning of Poultry
body_ar:
أفتى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء بموريتانيا قبل أيام في مسألة ذكاة الدواجن بعد صعقها، وكان ذلك ردا على استفسار ورد عدة مرات على موقع الشيخ يسأل أصحابه عن مدى حلية لحوم الدواجن التي تصعق قبل ذبحها، وذلك على أثر صدور قانون في فرنسا يفرض على أصحاب المجازر صعق الدواجن بالكهرباء قبل ذبحها..

فكانت فتوى الشيخ في المسألة واضحة حيث قال: " إذا كان الصعق يؤدي في بعض الأحيان إلى موتها ولو بنسبة ضئيلة فهي حرام، وإذا كان الصعق لا يؤدي إلى موتها بحال وإنما هو مجرد تخدير فلا يضر الذكاة".

يذكر في السياق ذاته أن مسألة ذكاة الدواجن المستوردة من أوربا والدول غير الإسلامية قد طرحت إشكالا عميقا ومتجددا في كل الأوقات حول هذه المسألة، وصدور هذا القانون في فرنسا يعيد طرح المسألة من جديد ويثير حولها الكثير من الالتباس لدى الرأي العام في الوطن الإسلامي، الذي تعتبر أغلب الدول الإسلامية فيه طرفا مستوردا للحوم من الدول غير الإسلامية، وتأتي هذه الفتوى من الشيخ في هذا الإطار، ورفعا للالتباس الذي يقع حولها.

وهذا نص السؤال وجواب الشيخ عليه:

السؤال:

السلام عليكم و رحمة الله وبركاته

عندي سؤال للشيخ محمد الحسن وهو أني أقيم في فرنسا وأملك دكان لبيع اللحوم الحلال ويزودني باللحم الحلال

مجزرة يديرها كافر والذي يذبح الدواجن مسلم إلا أنه مؤخرا صدر قانون يوجب على أصحاب المجازر أن يصعقوا الدواجن قبل ذبحها..

سؤالي هو هل هذه الدواجن حلال أم حرام ؟

الجواب:

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

وصلى الله على نبيه الكريم

إذا كان الصعق يؤدي في بعض الأحيان إلى موتها ولو بنسبة ضئيلة فهي حرام، وإذا كان الصعق لا يؤدي إلى موتها بحال وإنما هو مجرد تخدير فلا يضر الذكاة.
body_en:
His eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars in Mauritania, gave a fatwa some days ago on the question of the ritual slaughter (dhakāh) of poultry after they have been stunned. This was in answer to a query that had reached the Sheikh's website several times, its senders asking to what extent the meat of poultry that is stunned before being slaughtered is lawful — this following the issuing of a law in France requiring the owners of abattoirs to stun poultry with electricity before slaughtering them…

The Sheikh's fatwa on the question was clear. He said: "If the stunning leads in some instances to their death, even in a small proportion of cases, then they are forbidden (ḥarām); and if the stunning does not lead to their death at all, but is merely an anaesthetising, then it does no harm to the ritual slaughter."

We note in the same connection that the question of the ritual slaughter of poultry imported from Europe and from non-Muslim countries has at all times raised a deep and recurring difficulty, and that the issuing of this law in France raises the question afresh and stirs up much confusion about it in public opinion in the Muslim world, most of whose states are importers of meat from non-Muslim countries. The Sheikh's fatwa comes in this context, and in order to remove the confusion that arises around the matter.

This is the text of the question and of the Sheikh's answer to it:

The question:

Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

I have a question for Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan. It is that I live in France and own a shop selling halal meat, and I am supplied with halal meat by

an abattoir run by a non-Muslim, while the one who slaughters the poultry is a Muslim. Recently, however, a law was issued obliging the owners of abattoirs to stun the poultry before slaughtering them…

My question is: is this poultry lawful or forbidden?

The answer:

In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

And may God bless His noble Prophet.

If the stunning leads in some instances to their death, even in a small proportion of cases, then they are forbidden (ḥarām); and if the stunning does not lead to their death at all, but is merely an anaesthetising, then it does no harm to the ritual slaughter.

flags.arabic: إذا كان الصعق يؤدي … فهي حرام، وإذا كان الصعق لا يؤدي … فلا يضر الذكاة
flags.context: the ruling itself, given twice in the record
options: a conditional ruling with two branches, both of which must be displayed together
a ruling that stunned poultry is forbidden
a ruling that stunned poultry is permitted
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The ruling is conditional and has two branches, and the answer is worthless if either is shown without the other: if the stunning ever kills the bird, even rarely, the meat is forbidden (ḥarām); if it never kills but only anaesthetises, the ritual slaughter is unaffected. Any headline, excerpt, search snippet or social card drawn from this record must carry both branches. The Sheikh also does not decide the factual question of whether electrical stunning does in fact kill birds — that is left to the questioner — and no English wording may be allowed to suggest he decided it.

dhakāh is not in the glossary; a candidate for addition. It is the technical act that renders an animal lawful to eat, distinct from mere ذبح ('slaughtering'), which the same record also uses; the English keeps the two apart ('ritual slaughter' vs 'slaughtering'). 'Halal slaughter' has been avoided in the technical sentences because the record itself uses حلال separately, of the meat and of the shop.

flags.context: the questioner's description of his supplier
options: an abattoir run by a non-Muslim
an abattoir run by an unbeliever
an abattoir run by a kāfir
flags.note: EDITORIAL. kāfir here is a legal category in a slaughter question — who performs the slaughter determines the ruling — not an insult, and 'non-Muslim' carries that sense in plain English without importing an abusive register the Arabic does not have in this context. 'Unbeliever' is the literal option and is recorded; note that the same word is rendered 'unbeliever' in record 846, where the context is a biographical narrative rather than a slaughter ruling. A reviewer should settle a single corpus-wide policy.

flags.arabic: صدور قانون في فرنسا يفرض على أصحاب المجازر صعق الدواجن بالكهرباء قبل ذبحها
options: report the site's account of French law as the site gives it
verify and annotate the legal position
flags.note: EDITORIAL. The record's account of a 2013 French requirement to stun poultry is the site's, not the Sheikh's, and is not sourced. Pre-slaughter stunning and religious exemptions are live and litigated questions in French and EU law and in the halal certification trade; an English page stating what French law requires, under a scholar's name, carries both a factual-accuracy and a commercial exposure that the Arabic page does not. Translated as the source has it, with no legal claim added, verified or corrected.

flags.arabic: النص مصنف في القسم الإخباري رغم أنه فتوى كاملة بسؤالها وجوابها
flags.context: the CMS section of this record
options: record the CMS section as found and type the item by its content
re-file it under the written fatwas
flags.note: The CMS files this under 'news', but the record carries a complete written fatwa: the questioner's text and the Sheikh's answer, both verbatim, and the answer is given twice. It has therefore been typed 'fatwa' while section records the CMS location as found. Not re-filed unilaterally.

flags.context: the CMS timestamp on the record
options: treat as the date the item was uploaded to the CMS
treat as the date of composition
flags.note: CORPUS-WIDE DEFECT. The CMS serves a bulk-upload timestamp, not the date the Sheikh spoke or wrote. date_is_cms_upload is set true. Where the body itself names a date, that internal date is the better evidence and is kept in the English.

translator_notes: The answer appears twice in the record, once in the site's introduction and once as the text of the reply; the two differ only in the site's added spacing inside the quotation marks. Both are translated, and both must carry both branches of the condition.
أملك دكان is grammatically accusative where the syntax calls for a genitive (أملك دكانا); a source slip in the questioner's own writing, of no effect on sense.
أوربا is the source's spelling of أوروبا.
The site's '..' at two paragraph ends is its own punctuation, kept as an ellipsis.
